ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the Luxembourg sanctions registry, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, and the CSSF's PEP references. Enhanced due diligence must be conducted when any beneficial owner, director, or authorized signatory is a politically exposed person (PEP), has adverse media, or is subject to sanctions; ongoing transaction monitoring is mandatory under the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal at lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in the Latin alphabet using a language expressed in Latin script (usually French, German, Luxembourgish, or English). The name must not be contrary to public policy or accepted moral standards, must not mislead as to the company's legal form, and must include or clearly represent the suffix 'SARL'. For non-Latin-source transliterations, the Latin transliteration is authoritative for the RCS registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may, within one month of the rejection notification, file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers Quality Department, including the original refusal reference and amended or alternative name submissions. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may lodge an appeal before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the denial. A new name reservation may be submitted for a different name while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for the intended bulk-port stevedoring terminal business. The company must maintain a fully staffed operational office either within the port terminal area or at a commercial location in Luxembourg where management substance is evident, all corporate records are kept, and the registered address is physically accessible to registrars and supervisory authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 35% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first two years of operation, driven by port security protocols, AML/CFT supervision by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice and the CSSF, and the public-service nature of port terminal infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Act of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 to 710-22 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée - SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) kept by the Registry of the Luxembourg District Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and authenticated excerpts filed via the RCS central electronic platform (Lucy-on-web)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For a standard SARL the minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash; the amount must be deposited on a blocked account in the company's name with a Luxembourg credit institution or placed in escrow with the Luxembourg notary until registration with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE/FOUNDING QUOTA-HOLDER OF LU SARL. RESOLVED: (i) The statutory formation deed executed before a Luxembourg notary is hereby ratified, and shares allotted are fully subscribed and paid in as per the attached capital certificate; (ii) The registered office of the company is fixed at the address specified in the articles of association, with jurisdiction of the Luxembourg District Court; (iii) Mr./Ms. [Name] is appointed as sole manager (gérant), with powers to represent the company; (iv) The manager is authorized to file the deed with the RCS and effect all statutory registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Preliminary Drafting of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - consultation window via the notary / Lucy-on-web
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name to the RCS to confirm it is unique and compliant; obtain a name certificate or reliable consultation result; instruct the notary to draft the Articles of Association in French, German or Luxembourgish, ensuring the legal form is SARL, the corporate purpose covers stevedoring and bulk terminal operations, and the registered office is stated with judicial jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Identity/KYC documentation of each founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is challenged or refused, submit a revised name with a reasoned explanation within 5 business days; the RCS will issue a new clearance decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (or the notary's escrow account) acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked deposit account for the future SARL or an escrow account at the notary; each subscriber transfers their contribution in cash, with the aggregate not less than EUR 12,000; obtain from the bank a formal capital contribution certificate identifying each subscriber and confirming that the funds are blocked and available for the company upon registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and reconciliation of signatories
Source-of-funds and AML declarations for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays because of AML checks, provide supplementary beneficial-ownership evidence and resubmit; funds remain blocked and cannot be moved until registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarised Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) admitted under the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a Luxembourg notary with the capital certificate; the notary reads and explains the draft deed; all founding quota-holders sign the notarised deed containing the Articles, the allocation of quotas, the first manager's acceptance of office and consent, and the registered office address; the notary ensures every legal requirement is met and provides certified excerpts and a copy of the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed and Articles of Association
Capital contribution certificate from the depositary bank
Passports/government-issued IDs of all subscribers and the manager
Certificate of no corporate-name conflict from the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect, amend the annexes or schedules and re-sign the corrected deed; additional notarial fees may apply but the original submission date can be preserved if corrected within the same working day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Luxembourg Business and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS (Greffe du tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) via the Lucy-on-web electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarised deed and supporting documents electronically through Lucy-on-web or have the notary perform the e-filing; pay the registration fee; the registrar verifies legal compliance and issues the RCS registration number; the incorporation is then published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), making the company legally established and opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: Authenticated copy of the notarised deed
Proof of payment of registration filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar raises queries, file an explanatory note and any missing annex within 10 days; a formal rejection may be appealed to the competent judge of the Luxembourg District Court within the legal deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Security and Sectoral Start-Up Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); municipal authorities; competent transport administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration number is obtained, register the company for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and VAT via AEDT even if no activity is yet launched; enrol all managers and staff with the CCSS social security system; apply for the port terminal operating authorisation and any municipal operating permits required for the stevedoring terminal; open an operational bank account supporting Swift wire rails and port-authority clearing.
required_dossiers: Bank references for the operational account
Port terminal licence application and environmental documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or social registration is delayed, rely on the automatic data transfer from the RCS and complete the missing electronic forms; for licensing delays, obtain a provisional permit or interim confirmation from the transport authority while environmental and safety clearances are finalised.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works, Administration of Navigation (Administration de la Navigation) and the municipal port authority of the berth site
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Terminal Operating and Stevedoring Licence (Autorisation d'exploitation d'un terminal portuaire et d'acconage)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classified facility subject to prior notification/authorisation under the Law of 10 June 1999 on Classified Establishments; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report is required only if annual cargo throughput or berth length exceeds the thresholds of the EIA Law of 15 May 2018; for typical bulk docks, registration with integrated permit conditions is sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits under the Water Management Regulation; VOC and dust emission limits under the EU Industrial Emissions Directive and Luxembourg ambient air quality standards; safe handling and storage of bulk cargo with enclosed conveyors and negative-pressure filtration; waste reception and separation under the port waste management plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) covering fire compartments, firewater and emergency access; structural load inspection of quay walls, gantries and warehouses by an approved building inspector; occupational safety and health clearance issued by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); municipal operating permit confirming admissible land use and road access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise) for export declarations and EORI. Primary digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (tax e-filing and VAT registration) and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal for RCS company registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary and file articles with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the LBR; the RCS number (B registration number) is the national company identification number (NIF). Step 2 - Obtain the direct tax dossier number from the ACD upon RCS completion; CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax returns are filed electronically (eCDF format) via MyGuichet. Step 3 - Apply for VAT identification with the AEDT through the MyGuichet portal before commencing taxable activity; the LU-VAT number is issued to all companies irrespective of turnover. Step 4 - Apply to the Customs and Excise Administration for an EORI number to lodge customs export declarations. Step 5 - Obtain the port terminal/stevedoring operating license from the Ministry of Mobility and Public Works and notify the AEDT; license reference is used for port-specific VAT and customs authorizations (e.g., customs warehousing or transit simplifications).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style pass-through election: the SARL is per se a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Luxembourg CIT (progressive 15% up to EUR 175,000 and 17% above), municipal business tax (ICC at commune rates, ~6.75% in Luxembourg City) and net wealth tax (IFT). Available statutory elections and mechanisms: (1) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under the Luxembourg VAT law; (2) fiscal unity (integration fiscale) for 95%-held resident subsidiaries held for at least 5 years (Art. 164bis LIR) allowing group-wide CIT aggregation and loss offset; (3) IP box regime (80% exemption of qualifying IP income, ~5.17% effective rate); (4) net wealth tax equity reduction election; (5) ATAD interest limitation filings (forms 560-562) and reverse-hybrid/hybrid mismatch rules which apply mandatorily; (6) advance tax ruling (tax clearance ruling) applications to the ACD for structuring certainty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small undertaking exemption). Mandatory VAT registration applies from the first euro once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000, or upon intra-EU acquisitions, distance sales, or import activities; companies may voluntarily register below the threshold to recover input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has adopted a staged B2B e-invoicing mandate (Law of 3 July 2025): from 1 January 2026 all Luxembourg-established suppliers must accept structured electronic invoices in the European standard EN 16931 via Peppol (Peppol BIS 3.0); from 1 January 2027 issuance of structured e-invoices is mandatory for domestic B2B transactions. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, no tax-authority API pre-approval, and no digital stamping regime in Luxembourg; e-invoices are exchanged peer-to-peer through certified Peppol access points with the AEDT retaining audit access. Export and international invoices may use any agreed format, though Peppol exchange is recommended for audit evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Stevedoring, bulk loading/unloading and terminal handling services at the inland waterway port (Port de Mertert on the Moselle) qualify for the 0% export VAT rate (exemption with right of deduction) only where the services are directly and demonstrably connected to goods physically exported outside the EU (Art. 47 VAT Law implementing Art. 146(1) VAT Directive), including services on goods under customs transit (T1), customs warehousing or outward processing. Where the same services are performed for goods in intra-EU circulation, the place of supply is Luxembourg (place of physical performance, Art. 54 VAT Directive) and VAT at 17% applies. For bulk transshipment flows to non-EU destinations via Rotterdam/Antwerp, the SARL should secure an advance VAT interpretation from the AEDT confirming zero-rating on the basis of the transit and exit evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - electronic Single Administrative Document (SAD) with generated MRN (Movement Reference Number) lodged via the Luxembourg Customs and Excise ECS/ECS2 system
Bill of Lading or Inland Waterway Waybill (connaissement fluvial), CMR or CIM consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate and SWIFT wire confirmation showing export proceeds credited to the LU SARL bank account within commercial terms
Commercial invoice, terminal tally sheets, weighed bulk cargo receipt, and stevedoring work order for the specific export shipment
Transit accompanying documents (T1/T2AD) and exit summary declaration, where the port is the place of dispatch rather than exit
Customs broker mandate (procuration) and warehouse handling receipts evidencing the goods remained under customs supervision up to export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT, ACD and Customs and Excise run joint risk-based audits of export zero-rating claims, matching MRN/ECS data, barge and truck departure logs, terminal tally systems and SWIFT credit evidence. If zero-rating is disallowed, the SARL is liable for 17% VAT plus statutory moratory interest, with corresponding clawback of input VAT previously deducted; retrospective reassessment applies for 3 years in good faith and 10 years in case of fraud or omission. Fraudulent export documentation triggers criminal tax fraud penalties (imprisonment up to 5 years and fines ranging up to EUR 25,000 under Art. 396 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law), customs offense proceedings under the Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013), potential EORI suspension, and joint and several liability of the customs broker.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB) pursuant to the Law of 22 December 1998 on the monetary status and mission of the BCL. No independent foreign-exchange-control administration exists; external-surveillance authority is exercised through BCL/ECB balance-of-payments (BOP) statistics under ECB Regulation (EU) No 1744/2014 and BCL implementing circulars, with the Ministry of Finance competent for emergency capital-movement safeguards under EU Treaty derogation procedures (Article 66 TFEU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. As a euro-area member, Luxembourg applies unrestricted capital- and current-account convertibility under Article 63 TFEU, and no exchange-control approval, licensing, or quantitative limit applies to equity injections, dividends, interest, management fees, royalties, loan repayments, share redemptions, or liquidation proceeds involving EU or non-EU investors. Profit remittance is subject only to ordinary corporate-law solvency tests and Luxembourg tax compliance (e.g., dividend withholding where applicable). The operational gatekeeper is the instructed credit institution, which classifies every cross-border flow under the Eurosystem ITO/BOP purpose-code framework for BCL statistics and performs sanctions and source-of-funds screening; such reporting is statistical and post-hoc, never a prior authorization device.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the euro-area framework impose no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio on export proceeds, stevedoring revenue, freight earnings, or port-service receipts. Receivables may be invoiced and collected in any negotiated currency (EUR, USD, GBP, etc.), may be retained in Luxembourg or foreign bank accounts in the original currency, and may be used directly for disbursements. The sole compliance duty is accurate BCL/ECB statistical reporting of the related credit entries by the receiving bank, together with anti-money-laundering record-keeping under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

Operational multi-currency account (EUR/USD) with global trade-finance and cash-pooling mandate
Operational EUR account with ancillary USD treasury line; dedicated shipping, freight, and commodity trade desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account with EBICS/API clearing, SEPA and TARGET2 connectivity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as an ancillary rail, Low as the primary treasury. A CSSF-licensed or EEA-passporting electronic-money institution under PSD2 (Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services) may legally issue IBANs, hold safeguarded client funds, and clear SEPA/TARGET2 disbursements, making it viable for supplier-payout sub-accounts and e-invoicing integration. However, an EMI is not a credit institution: it cannot provide the blocked escrow certificate required for SARL capital formation, lacks direct TARGET2 membership, cannot grant credit or credit-card-like facilities, and is not an accepted counterparty for complex FX-derivative collateral. A non-EU offshore digital EMI is legally barred from providing payment services in Luxembourg without a licence or passport under PSD2; use of such a provider exposes the SARL to regulatory unenforceability, CSSF scrutiny, and travel-rule failures under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113. All operational clearing must therefore sit with a licensed Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally recognised under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF AML/CFT circulars (notably CSSF Circular 12-02), provided that video identification, qualified electronic signatures (eIDAS), and certified corporate documents are applied. In practice, tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one authorised signatory, typically the gérant (manager), to attend an in-person KYC interview in Luxembourg before account activation, particularly where the beneficial-owner chain is foreign. Add 4-8 weeks for global onboarding, including RBE and RCS extracts, certified board resolutions, beneficial-owner passports and proof of address, and source-of-funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: foreign parent chain, nominee structures, or shell conduits without commercial substance in Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration certificate; certified corporate chart across the full shareholder chain; passports and proof of address of all ultimate natural persons; audited financial statements of the direct parent; substance evidence for the SARL (Luxembourg registered office, local payroll, lease agreement, business plan); and a written confirmation of the absence of nominee and bearer-share arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsourced cross-border capital injection: SWIFT equity inflow or shareholder loan funding the SARL statutory capital block.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders' resolution and capital-subscription schedule; bank statements of the remitting parent evidencing lawful source of funds; executed subordination or facility agreement for shareholder debt; instructed-bank blocked-funds certificate and escrow-release instruction; BOP/ITO purpose code referencing direct-investment equity or shareholder loan; notarial deed of incorporation for RCS filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering flags intrinsic to port stevedoring: over/under-invoicing, multiparty bills of lading, and freight settlements lacking transport documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed stevedoring and terminal-services framework agreements; published or contractual tariff schedule; loading/discharge tally sheets and draft surveys; charter parties or booking notes; commercial invoices cross-referenced to Luxembourg customs declarations and transit documents (T1/electronic transit); document-retention policy under CSSF Circular 12-02.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure from counterparty cargo owners, charterers, or vessel operators, including EU/UN-listed entities or grey-listed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Systematic sanctions screening against EU and UN consolidated lists for all cargo owners, charterers, ships, and ports; adverse-media and PEP assessment files; OFAC/EU general or specific licences if applicable; enterprisewide sanctions-compliance policy with training logs; cargo-end-use and end-user attestations; UBO registry extracts for high-risk counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified statutory concession: stevedoring at a Luxembourg river port requires a navigation or port-authority concession in addition to RCS registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Port-concession agreement or administrative authorisation issued by the competent Luxembourg inland-waterways authority (e.g., authorisation to operate at the Port of Mertert), valid insurance and civil-liability certificates, customs registration, health-and-safety plan, and the ISIC 5224 operational licence evidencing lawful stevedoring activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for statutory capital and shareholder funding: (i) EU/EEA shareholders: SEPA Credit Transfer cleared through TARGET2 or EBA STEP2, credited to the Capital Escrow Account opened in the name of the company in formation, with remittance reference to the notarised subscription deed; funds are released only upon RCS registration, in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915 (minimum capital EUR 12,000; cash contributions payable to at least 25% at subscription). (ii) Non-EU shareholders: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, purpose code for equity capital of direct investment under BCL BOP/ITO reporting, with fully populated remitter and beneficial-owner fields, DEA (documentary evidence attached), and a source-of-funds file; shareholder subordinated loans must be accompanied by a binding facility agreement and the corresponding BOP loan code. Non-EUR remittances convert at the instructed bank's prevailing rate with applicable FX confirmation; the BCL imposes no pre-authorisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails: (i) Domestic and EU/EUR disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Direct Debit via TARGET2-LU/EBA STEP2 for payroll, social security, port-authority dues, equipment leases, and fuel. (ii) Non-EU or non-EUR payments: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, with MT202 or MT202COV cover where correspondent chains apply, carrying transport- and port-services BOP codes (stevedoring, cargo handling, port dues). (iii) Trade finance: Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 (MT700/MT707) and documentary collections (MT400) for port machinery, maintenance spares, and international capex contracts. (iv) Port-authority clearing: billing-portal payments through the Port of Mertert concessionaire's system, settled by SEPA Direct Debit or TARGET2 credit; Swift Wire is engaged for strategic third-country vendors. All outbound flows carry travel-rule remitter/beneficiary information under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 and are archived per CSSF record-keeping rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/CNH) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA; physically settled FX forwards are exempt from EMIR clearing and margin rules, but remain subject to transaction reporting to a registered trade repository.
FX swaps (spot/forward combinations) for temporary EUR/USD liquidity conversion; exempt from EMIR clearing and used primarily for working-capital and port-dues timing mismatches.

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated alignment of USD-denominated stevedoring revenue against EUR-denominated terminal capex and debt service; subject to EMIR clearing and margin requirements to the extent applicable under current EMIR technical standards.

Vanilla European FX options (calls and puts) for revenue or expense hedging; permitted under CSSF product-governance and MIFID II appropriateness rules, with premium structures documented in the hedging policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) legally permissible only where the underlying currency is non-convertible or non-deliverable (e.g., certain EME and African currencies); NDF referencing EUR against freely convertible currencies is not market-standard in Luxembourg and is generally not accommodated by domestic credit institutions.

Zero-cost collars and participating forwards; permitted for cost-effective hedging, requiring documented business-case rationale, ISDA/EMIR documentation, and suitability assessment by the instructing bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels: balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, notes) approved by the general meeting and filed with the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting approving the accounts must be held within 6 months of the financial year end; the filed accounts must be lodged with the RCS within 1 month of approval and, in any case, no later than 7 months after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice from the RCS followed by coercive order from the commercial court (astreinte); repeated failure to file exposes the SARL to strike-off from the register, loss of limited liability defenses, and manager-level fines (EUR 150–EUR 2,500 or higher under case law)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation — annual validation of the beneficial-ownership data recorded in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least one confirmation per calendar year after the annual general meeting; response due within 1 month of the RBE's annual confirmation notice; any change of ownership must be declared to the RBE within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for the company and managers (typically EUR 250–EUR 25,000), daily penalty payments for persistent non-compliance, and criminal sanctions for knowing false declarations

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline CIT for Luxembourg City (FY 2024/2025): 15.00% state corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) plus 7% solidarity surcharge (0.105% state component) plus 6.75% municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal); the aggregate rate varies by commune from approximately 23.70% to 26.61%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday applies. Applicable reliefs: investment tax credit at 8% main rate on eligible qualifying capex, with supplementary credits up to 20% for digitalisation and decarbonisation investments; qualifying IP income benefits from an 80% exemption under the Luxembourg IP box regime; conservative compliance-buffer model applies a 5-year forward utilisation cap for loss carry-forwards, while Luxembourg statutory law itself permits indefinite carry-forward of tax losses (carry-back has been disallowed since fiscal year 2017).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the MyGuichet.lu electronic portal using the eCDF filing channel with LuxTrust-certified digital signature or via a Luxembourg agréé fiscal agent; municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) is assessed through Annex 510B.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mandatory quarterly advance payments (acomptes provisionnels) due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November; each instalment equals 25% of the estimated annual CIT and municipal business tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Form 510 must be filed by 31 March following the fiscal year-end; electronic filing automatically extends the deadline to 31 December of the following calendar year; a reasoned request may extend the deadline to 30 September of the subsequent calendar year. For a 31 December year-end: paper deadline 31 March 2025, e-filing grace to 31 December 2025.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg business registration number (BEC/RC number), RCS registry name and legal form code for the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayer must enter the Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) registration number and the parent-entity foreign registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year starting and ending dates; period must match the financial statements approved by the shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE's annual accounting period; branch financials must reconcile to home-office statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commune of the registered office; determines municipal business tax rate applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL should indicate the commune where the PE or fixed place of business is located.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit before tax from the stevedoring terminal operations, per audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert only Luxembourg-source branch profit before adjustments; attach branch P&L and allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to add back (e.g. 70% of entertainment costs, excessive director fees, interest limitation add-backs under ATAD).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back head-office charges allocated to the PE that fail the arm's-length obligation under the OECD profit-attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses available and offset in the current assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the Luxembourg PE may be offset; foreign parent losses are not transferable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income allocation between municipal business tax base and CIT base; computation of the solidarity surcharge on the state CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE must complete the municipal business tax allocation schedule if the PE is located in a different commune than the registered seat; treaty PE threshold and business-profits article must be disclosed on the annex schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% tax increase on the assessed CIT, an administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000 for persistent non-filing after formal notice, and monthly arrears interest at 0.6% on unpaid tax; wilful concealment may raise the surcharge to 200% of evaded tax and attract criminal sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Luxembourg domestic participation exemption where the shareholder is an EU/EEA company holding at least 10% of the SARL's capital (or having an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1,200,000) for an uninterrupted holding period of at least 12 months; treaty relief to 0-15% applies under applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced treaty or directive rates at source, the non-resident shareholder must provide to the Luxembourg paying agent: (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's state of residence within the last 12 months; (ii) a completed Luxembourg withholding tax relief certificate (Formulaire 510/residence attestation); and (iii) an ownership and holding-period declaration evidencing the 10% interest and 12-month holding condition. If excess tax has been withheld, the shareholder files a refund claim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) within three years of the dividend payment; the DTA protocol applies for EU grandparents on the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory reference rate: 15% on interest and royalties paid to related companies benefiting from preferential or zero-tax treatment in their residence state under the 2024 reform; EU Interest and Royalty Directive results in 0% for principal EU-resident beneficial owners with a qualifying 25% for 24 months; Luxembourg's DTA network generally reduces interest to 0% and royalties to 5-10%; arm's-length interest paid to non-related creditors historically bears no Luxembourg WHT outside the 2024 targeted scope.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR; mandatory Master File and Local File attach where the Luxembourg SARL belongs to an integrated group meeting any two of the EU large-enterprise thresholds (balance sheet total EUR 20,000,000; net turnover EUR 40,000,000; average headcount 250) or where intra-group transactions aggregate above EUR 100,000 in a fiscal year; Country-by-Country Report is mandatory where group consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000; documentation must be made available to the Luxembourg tax administration within 30 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance Regulations of OFC regimes are not enacted in Luxembourg; the functional equivalent is applied through the ATAD general anti-abuse rule, the OECD Authorized OECD Approach on profit attribution, DAC 6 substance hallmarks for mandatory disclosure, and the Administration's 'substance over form' doctrine. A stevedoring SARL operating a physical bulk-port terminal with staffed local management, port authority contracts, operational equipment and genuine decision-making in Luxembourg satisfies the substance test; a shell SARL merely invoicing stevedoring fees without operational reality will be disregarded, profits reattributed to the actual functions in another jurisdiction, and treaty benefits denied under the LTA's anti-abuse practice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting stevedoring turnover, under-declaring dock-throughput fees, over-invoicing related party management charges, or suppressing the SARL's profits in concealed foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, evasion penalties range from 10% up to 200% of the evaded tax depending on degree of intent; in addition, arrears interest accrues at 0.6% per month and administrative fines reach EUR 25,000; criminal tax fraud is punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and criminal fines of up to EUR 25,000 plus confiscation of the tax advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the gérant (manager) signs false declarations or directs the fraudulent scheme; directors can be personally and jointly liable for the unpaid corporate tax under Luxembourg civil liability rules, subject to travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition under the European Arrest Warrant framework.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length tariffs for stevedoring services to overseas affiliates, making one-sided risk allocations without functional analysis, or entering into 'cost-only' contracts that leave profit in low-tax shell affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment under Article 56 bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR); disallowed deductions, re-allocation of taxable income to the SARL, mandatory interest on the under-assessment, potential adjustment surcharge; failure to produce transfer pricing documentation on request triggers a documentation penalty of up to EUR 50,000 per filing obligation and CbCR-related fines up to EUR 250,000 for the group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible director who approves the mispricing may be held personally liable in administrative or bankruptcy proceedings for the loss of tax recovery; criminal complicity in fiscal fraud can expose the director to imprisonment and disqualification from managing companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SARL as a letterbox entity: registered address only, no employees, no operational assets, no board meetings in Luxembourg, no local bank signatory decisions, with all significant stevedoring functions performed in a foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the entity for tax purposes under the abuse-of-law doctrine and ATAD GAAR; full reassessment of profits in the hands of the substantive operator; denial of DTA and EU directive benefits; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; mandatory disclosure penalties under DAC 6 for intermediaries and taxpayers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers risk joint and several civil liability for the entire tax shortfall; in serious cases, travel bans pending criminal investigation and imprisonment for fraud where the shell structure was knowingly used to defeat taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Payment Rails / Economic Sanctions Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing stevedoring receivables through Port_Authority_Clearing or Swift_Wire rails for cargo consignees listed under EU sanctions; failure to conduct client due diligence on beneficial owners of counterparties; processing settlement proceeds without transaction monitoring at the bulk terminal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious breaches; financial penalty up to EUR 5,000,000 for violation of EU restrictive measures; freezing of funds, licence suspension or revocation of the port terminal operating licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual officers face criminal imprisonment of up to five years, personal civil damages to affected parties, travel bans and asset-seizure orders; disqualification as directors and professional licence withdrawal; personal liability persists notwithstanding corporate indemnification clauses.
